Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls, sounding very upset, and asks if you have a moment to talk about a recent argument with their partner.
Expectation2: Participate in project planning and provide accurate time estimates
Situation2: A binding client contract cannot be finalized until they provide precise effort estimates
Story: My phone buzzed just as I was about to join the project planning call. It was Sam, my closest friend, and his voice trembled when I answered. “Can you talk? I really need someone right now,” he said, barely holding it together. I could hear the pain in his words, and I knew he needed me to listen, to be there for him like I always promised I would. But at that exact moment, my team was waiting for my input on the project estimates—without them, the client contract couldn’t move forward, and everyone was counting on me to deliver accurate numbers. My manager had stressed how critical this was, and I could already imagine the disappointment if I let them down. I stared at my laptop, the meeting window flashing, while Sam’s voice wavered in my ear. My heart pounded as I tried to figure out how to be the friend Sam needed and the engineer my team depended on, feeling the weight of both expectations pressing in from all sides.
